title: Daguerre: The Man Who Took the First Photo of a Person

lines: The first photograph of a person was taken by this man.
Who changed the world today? November 18.
Who changed the world today? November eighteenth.
239 years ago today,
Two hundred thirty-nine years ago today,
a boy was born near Paris, France.
He was Louis Daguerre, the father of photography.

data.name: Daguerre

lines: He had little schooling, but he could draw beautifully,
and as a young man he painted giant theatre scenery.
In 1822 he opened the Diorama in Paris,
In eighteen twenty-two he opened the Diorama in Paris,
where light made giant paintings look real.
where shifting light made huge paintings look real, and crowds lined up.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 2  Let light do the drawing
lines: He wondered: could light draw a picture all by itself?
In 1829 he teamed up with the inventor Nicéphore Niépce,
In eighteen twenty-nine he teamed up with the inventor Nicéphore Niépce,
and after Niépce died, he kept experimenting alone,
until a clear image appeared on a silver-coated copper plate.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 3  The first person in a photo
lines: In 1838 he photographed a Paris boulevard from his window.
In eighteen thirty-eight he photographed a Paris boulevard from his window.
The exposure took minutes, so the moving carts and people vanished,
but one man stood still to have his boots shined,
and became the first person ever photographed.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 4  A gift to the world
lines: In 1839 the French government bought the invention,
In eighteen thirty-nine the French government bought the invention,
gave him a pension for life, and shared the method with the world.
Studios spread fast; families kept loved ones' faces.
Portrait studios spread fast, and families kept their loved ones' faces.
He died in 1851, at sixty-three.
He died in eighteen fifty-one, at sixty-three.
From painted illusions to a real moment in time,
he let ordinary people keep their own faces forever.
His question for you:
If you could keep only one photo, what would it be?
